evidence: ACIP in C05:171 reads SKYES MYOD MI BYED, and the wylie preserves myod, so this is not a converter-only discrepancy. The next verse line in this same segment has myong mi byed. The commentary on this line at C05:173 has skyes nas myong 'gyur gyi las mi byed and English 'does no deeds of the type that will lead to an experience there after being reborn'. The current dictionary has no exact myod entry; myong has HGM 'experience' and records tenses myong / myong / myangs/ myongs. Read-only queries for wylie 'byis pa der skyes', wylie 'myod mi byed', and English 'A stable child does none' each return only C05:171: no other witness to this verse was found, including C16. The historical assertion that myod is unique across the corpus is incorrect: TCS10:338 also has myod yul, later myong yul, and English about an object experienced. That is a different passage and is not independent testimony to this verse. The proposed restoration follows the internal parallel and commentary; no blockprint was checked, so confidence remains PROBABLE. Current errata_register.json, ERRATA_REGISTER.md, BACKLOG.md and TODO.md contain no matching record. Registered converter, footnote, heading, folio, row-spill and English-cap classes do not explain MYOD.
